questions.question: What is the required `track` expression in `@for` used for?
options: Logging performance metrics to the console
Letting Angular match items across re-renders by a stable identity instead of recreating DOM nodes
questions.explanation: Similar to React's `key`, `track` tells Angular how to identify items between renders so it can reuse DOM nodes instead of destroying and recreating them.

questions.question: When should you prefer `[class.active]="isActive"` over `[ngClass]`?
options: When you only need to toggle a single class, since it avoids importing NgClass
class binding doesn't support boolean expressions
questions.explanation: For a single conditional class, the lightweight class binding syntax does the job without pulling in the NgClass directive.

questions.question: What does the `async` pipe do differently from manually calling `.subscribe()` in a component?
options: It converts the Observable into a synchronous value
It automatically subscribes and unsubscribes, preventing memory leaks
It disables change detection for that binding
questions.explanation: The async pipe manages the subscription lifecycle tied to the template, cleaning up automatically when the component is destroyed.

questions.question: By default, when does Angular re-run a pipe's `transform` method?
options: On every change detection cycle, regardless of input
Only when the input reference changes (pure pipes)
questions.explanation: Pipes are pure by default — Angular skips re-running transform unless the input value/reference actually changes, keeping them cheap even in loops.
